  • Oxidative Addition: C–H Bond Activation by Fe(CO)4

Oxidative Addition: C–H Bond Activation by Fe(CO)4#

Introduction#

Oxidative addition is a common step in transition-metal catalysis. In the reaction considered here, Fe(CO)4 activates a C–H bond of methane, leading to cleavage of the bond and the formation of the oxidative addition product.

In this example, we examine the oxidative addition transition state studied by Sun et al. [1] The analysis identifies two complementary interactions: donation from methane to Fe(CO)4 and backdonation from Fe(CO)4 to methane. [2]

Usage#

Load the calculation#

  1. Download the example file: Oxidative_Addition.adf.rkf.

  2. Open PyOrbb and drag the .rkf file into the application.

  3. Uncheck Show PR to hide the Pauli-repulsive interactions.

Two main orbital interactions should appear in the interaction diagram.

View the orbitals#

  1. Select an orbital in the interaction diagram.

  2. Click the orbital-viewer control labelled φ.

The PyOrbb viewer opens with options for displaying the orbital. Inspect the methane and Fe(CO)4 orbitals involved in each interaction, using a viewing direction that clearly shows the activating C–H bond and the iron centre.

Analysis#

PyOrbb identifies two strong interactions between the fragments that were also identified by Sun, et al. The first is between the occupied CH4(5A) and the virtual Fe(CO)4(42A) FMOs. This is the C–H \(\sigma\)-donation interaction: electrons are donated from the bonding orbital of methane to the iron fragment. The other interaction occurs between the occupied Fe(CO)4(41A) and the virtual CH4(6A) FMOs and is the backdonation interaction with electrons being donated from Fe(CO)4 into CH4.

References#

[1]

X. Sun, M. V. J. Rocha, T. A. Hamlin, J. Poater, and F. M. Bickelhaupt, “Understanding the differences between iron and palladium in cross-coupling reactions,” Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 2019, 9651–9664. DOI: 10.1039/C8CP07671E.

[2]

Y. Hordijk, S. E. Beutick, X. Sun, L. Groot, T. Gijzen, J. Poater, T. A. Hamlin, F. M. Bickelhaupt, C. Fonseca Guerra, “PyOrbb – Automated Analyses of Orbital-Interaction Mechanisms” J. Comput. Chem., 2026, e70512, DOI: https://doi.org/10.1002/jcc.70512.
